summaryBox.title: Van 't Hoff Factor
summaryBox.takeaway: i = Observed / Calculated Colligative Property = M_calc / M_obs. Dissociation: α = (i-1)/(n-1). Association (dimer): β = 2(1-i).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
VAN 'T HOFF FACTOR (i) EQUATIONS

• i = Observed Colligative Property / Calculated Colligative Property
• i = Calculated (Theoretical) Molar Mass / Observed (Experimental) Molar Mass

1. Dissociation (i > 1, e.g., K₄[Fe(CN)₆] ⟹ n = 5):
   α = (i - 1) / (n - 1) ⟹ i = 1 + (n - 1)α

2. Association (i < 1, e.g., Dimerization of Benzoic Acid in Benzene ⟹ n = 2):
   β = (1 - i)n / (n - 1) ⟹ β = 2(1 - i)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Dissociation ($i > 1$)**: For an electrolyte yielding $n$ ions, $i = 1 + (n - 1)\alpha \implies \alpha = \frac{i - 1}{n - 1}$.
• **Association ($i < 1$)**: For $n$ molecules associating to form an $n$-mer, $i = 1 + (\frac{1}{n} - 1)\beta \implies \beta = \frac{(1 - i)n}{n - 1}$. For dimerization ($n=2$), $\beta = 2(1 - i)$.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
10 NEST TRAPS SUMMARY

1. Higher K_H indicates LOWER gas solubility.
2. Minimum boiling azeotropes (95.6% ethanol) cannot be separated by fractional distillation.
3. Non-volatile solutes ALWAYS depress freezing points.
4. BaCl₂ has n = 3 ions (i = 3 for 100% dissociation).
5. Colligative order: CaCl₂ (i=3) > NaCl (i=2) > Glucose (i=1).
6. Osmotic pressure uses Molarity (M), not molality.
7. Reverse Osmosis requires external P > Π.
8. Acetone + Chloroform exhibits Negative Deviation due to H-bonding.
9. Molarity decreases upon heating (volume expands).
10. RLVP equals the Mole Fraction of SOLUTE (x_B), not solvent.
